title: Harrington's global-economy reason for secrecy
summary: Brent Friedman tells of Harrington's global-economy reason for secrecy, about 1981 at United States (no place named), and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: That's the global economy. If you disrupt that by taking away the reason for people to live their lives, everything falls apart and governments of the world will not be able to control the populace.

plain: Brent Friedman, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says a man named John Harrington, presented in the episode's title as a former US Secretary of Energy, told him why the government keeps contact with non-human intelligence secret, in a conversation set around 1981. As Friedman tells it, Harrington said the reason is the global economy: if people lost their reason for living their everyday lives, everything would fall apart and governments could no longer control the population. If true, it would mean secrecy is kept to protect the world's economic order.
